messages:
marie: Usability quick-check for the new metric card: when cards are narrow the legend wraps and the axis units push the sparkline down. Two separate debates: 1) how to present units/percentiles in the constrained legend area; 2) how to surface anomalies without hiding raw spikes. Brainstorming options: condensed legend tokens + popover, single-line legend with ellipsis + accessible tooltip, or inline tiny sparkline preview with separate detailed view. Also smoothing: median vs gaussian kernel?

sam: For the legend, I prefer tokenized entries (e.g., `p95 · ms`) so each legend line stays short. Popover that opens on click for full metric name is good for touch. Avoid hover-only.

alex: Smoothing: median filter is robust to spikes but can remove narrow peaks. Gaussian (or exponential smoothing) keeps trend shape but can smear. Recommend median for anomaly-sensitive dashboards and gaussian for trend-focused views. Expose a small toggle with labels `Smoothing (median)` vs `Smoothing (gaussian)`? Maybe too much complexity.

toni: Accessibility: if you abbreviate tokens, provide aria-label with full wording: "95th percentile latency (p95) in milliseconds". For popovers, ensure keyboard access and that the popover content is reachable by screen readers. Also legends need logical tab order.

lars: Anomalies: instead of dimming we could outline outliers with a hollow circle + an explicit legend item `○ anomaly`. Clicking the legend item filters the chart to show only anomalies. That helps surface them rather than conceal.

marie: I like outline markers. What about clustering markers when multiple anomalies are dense? We could show a small cluster badge `+3` and expand on click. Also need to think about export: users want an anomalies CSV.

sam: Good point on CSV. UX: toggle `Highlight anomalies` in the chart toolbar. When on, markers appear and a small inline list shows top 5 anomalies for the selected timeframe. When off, keep lines undimmed — dimming feels like data loss.

alex: Implementation note: computing gaussian kernels client-side might be heavier. Median of 3/5 points is cheap. Maybe default to median with a setting to enable gaussian smoothing for longer time series. Also include a microcopy tooltip: `Smoothing (reduce noise). Median smoothing preserves sharp spikes.`

toni: Tooltip + aria-describedby for the toggle. For legend tokens, use visually condensed text but in the DOM include a visually-hidden element with the full metric name for SR users. Example SR string: "Latency, 95th percentile, p95, measured in milliseconds".

marie: Action items: (1) I'll design a token legend variant + popover prototype showing full metric info and copy for the anomaly CSV link; (2) alex/sam please confirm median window (3 vs 5) and perf constraints; (3) toni will draft aria strings for legend/popover and cluster badges. Preview bot will upload prototypes.

preview-bot: Prototype: https://staging.redwood.ai/proto/legend-tokens-clusters (expires 24h)

marie: Thanks. I'll post mocks and the exact SR copy in ~2 hours.
